The BSL Licensor covenants in lines 28–31 impose operative duties on the Licensor, but the fixed activity vocabulary has no faithful action for specifying license terms, setting the Change Date, or refraining from other license modifications.

paragraph_audit.reason: The earlier-of triggers grant rights under the Change License and terminate the original paragraph 6 rights; the Change License terms are not supplied, so its specific permissions and conditions are not inferred.

Line 22 grants conditional permission to use the License text to license one's works and to refer to it by the trademark, subject to the identified Covenants of Licensor. The condition's application to the recipient remains unclear because the supplied covenants state duties of the Licensor.

Lines 28–31 impose operative administrative duties on the Licensor: specify a qualifying Change License, specify an Additional Use Grant or insert 'None', specify a Change Date, and not otherwise modify the License. These actions do not fit an existing activity. Lines 32–34 are standard header text and add no separate behavioral duty.

Line 38 states that on the date above use will be governed by the open source license specified in LICENSE.TXT; the referenced license is not supplied and its terms are excluded. The local changeover statement is captured by the cited anchor, without inferring the missing license's contents.

additional_anchor_review.reason: Line 6 expressly grants copying of the Licensed Work, subject to the changeover in line 8.
Line 6 expressly grants modification of the Licensed Work, subject to the changeover in line 8.
Line 6 expressly grants creation of derivative works, subject to the changeover in line 8.
Line 6 expressly grants redistribution of the Licensed Work, subject to the changeover in line 8.
Line 6 grants non-production use and says an Additional Use Grant may permit limited production use.
Line 8 grants rights under the Change License subject to its terms; it does not establish an unconditional PERMITTED Use. The Change License's actual scope and conditions are not supplied.

Line 8 ends the rights granted in line 6, not every possible Use of the Licensed Work. The anchor's Use prohibition should be limited to the original BSL grant; independent rights under the Change License are not barred. The added clauses represent the ending of the paragraph 6 rights for the other expressly granted activities.
Line 10 expressly requires purchase of a commercial license or refraining from use when use fails to comply with currently effective requirements; the alternatives are disjunctive.
Line 12 applies the License separately to each version and to copies of original and modified Licensed Work and derivative works.
Line 14 expressly requires conspicuous display of the License on each original or modified copy.
Line 14 states that the License terms apply to use when the work is received from a third party in original or modified form.

Line 16 says a violating use automatically terminates rights for current and all other versions. The anchor represents this as a PROHIBITED Use, which can misleadingly describe termination as a use prohibition; the source states an effect on rights, not a distinct prohibition or cure rule.
Line 18 expressly withholds trademark and logo rights except where their use is expressly required by the License.

Line 22 expressly grants conditional permission to use the License text to license works and to refer to it using the Business Source License trademark. The condition is stated, though its application is unclear.

Lines 28–31 are operative Licensor covenants, but the anchor encodes them as an UNSPECIFIED Use clause. The duties concern specifying license terms and a date and not modifying the License, rather than a licensee Use action; they are classified OUTSIDE_ACTIVITY_SCOPE.

Line 38 is a statement that use will be governed by the open source license specified in LICENSE.TXT on the date above, not an UNSPECIFIED Use constraint. The referenced license and date value are unavailable; the missing license is excluded rather than inferred.
